# Apocalypse of Peter — Chapter 1
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Source:** Akhmim Fragment / Ethiopic MS, Apocalypse of Peter 1

---

1. And as he sat upon the Mount of Olives, his own disciples came to him, and we besought him and implored him one by one and entreated him, saying to him: "Make known to us what are the signs of your coming and of the end of the world."

2. And our Lord answered and said to us: "Take heed that no man lead you astray. Many shall come in my name saying, 'I am the Christ.' Believe them not, and draw not near to them."

3. "For there shall come forth the deceivers and false prophets, and they shall set up instructions and diverse doctrines, ensnaring those who are perishing."

4. "And they shall be sons of perdition. And then shall God come, my Father, to raise the dead and to judge the living and the dead and to reward every man according to his deeds."

5. And he showed us in his right hand the souls of all men, and upon the palm of his right hand the image of that which shall be accomplished at the last day.

6. And I saw how the wicked were delivered to the angels of punishment, who drove them to a place of outer darkness.

7. He said to us: "When the fig tree has put forth its shoots, in the last days shall deceivers and false prophets arise and shall expound diverse doctrines to the ensnaring of those who are perishing."

8. "And the parable of the fig tree — understand it thus: when its shoots have sprung forth and its boughs grown, the end of the world shall come."

9. And I, Peter, answered and said to him: "Explain to me also the parable of the fig tree. How shall we understand it?"

10. And the Lord answered me and said: "Do you not understand that the fig tree is the house of Israel? As a man planted a fig tree in his garden, and it brought forth no fruit, and he sought its fruit for many years. And when he found it not, he said to the keeper of his garden: 'Root up this fig tree that it water not our ground to no purpose.'"

11. "And the keeper of the garden said to him: 'Suffer us to root it up yet once more and to dig around it and to water it, and if it bring not forth fruit we will straightway remove its roots from the garden and plant another tree in its place.'"

12. "Have you not understood that the fig tree is the house of Israel? Verily I say to you, when its boughs have sprouted forth in the last days, then shall deceitful Christs come and awaken hope saying, 'I am the Christ who am now come into the world.'"

13. "And when they shall see the wickedness of their deeds, even of the false Christs, they shall turn away after them and deny him to whom our fathers gave praise, the first Christ whom they crucified and thereby sinned greatly."

14. "But this deceiver is not the Christ. And when they reject him, he shall slay with the sword, and there shall be many martyrs."

15. Then shall the boughs of the fig tree, that is, the house of Israel, shoot forth; and there shall be many martyrs by his hand: they shall be killed and become martyrs.

16. "Enoch and Elijah shall be sent to instruct them that this is the Deceiver who must come into the world and do signs and wonders in order to deceive."

17. "And therefore shall they that die by his hand be martyrs and shall be reckoned among the good and righteous martyrs who have pleased God in their lives."

---
*EMET renders the Greek Akhmim text closely, with Ethiopic variants noted where divergence is significant. Verse divisions follow Klostermann's enumeration.*
